observations: Ergonomic office chair with a mesh backrest and a headrest.
The chair is shown in an extremely reclined, almost horizontal position.
Five-star chrome base with black casters.
Visible white marks or dust on the headrest in photo 0.

claims.evidence: Unclear if 'Bent' refers to a brand or the reclined state shown in the photo.
Photo 0 is taken from too far away to confirm; there appear to be light marks on the headrest.
Resolution of photo 0 is insufficient to inspect the mesh and fabric integrity.
The seller provided verbal assurance but no visual evidence of the chair's mechanical functions.

risks.risk: The recline mechanism may be broken or unable to lock upright, given the extreme angle shown.
risks.proof: A video showing the backrest being moved and locked into a standard upright position.

risks.risk: The gas lift (height adjustment) may be non-functional.
risks.proof: A video showing the chair being raised and lowered while someone is seated.
risks.if_unproven: as having a failed gas lift

risks.risk: The casters (wheels) may be seized or damaged.
risks.proof: A video of the chair being rolled across the floor.
risks.if_unproven: as needing a full set of replacement wheels

proof_requests: Video of the backrest locking in the upright position.
Video of the gas lift adjusting the height up and down.
Close-up photos of the seat fabric and the mesh back to check for stains or snags.
Video of the chair rolling on its wheels.
response.reason: The seller's verbal confirmation does not replace visual proof of mechanical function. The chair is priced at its worst case (non-functional) because it is only shown in an extreme recline and the gas lift is untested.
